lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Check that the contact details are real, professional, and accessible.
items.because: They look like placeholders unless they were anonymized for review.

items.says: Make sure the expected graduation date is current when you apply.
Clarify what owning the websites and component library meant and what you personally delivered.
items.because: The scope is broad, but the technical contribution is unclear.

items.says: Substantiate the link between the interviews, preview mode, and reduction in broken pages.
items.because: The claimed connection needs support.

items.says: Define “broken pages” and explain how the monthly counts were measured.
Clarify the audits, their scope, and whether the before-and-after counts are comparable.
items.because: The reader needs to understand the measurement.

items.says: Define “search time,” how it was tested, and the size or nature of the catalog.
items.because: It is unclear whether this was a measured user outcome or a local performance test.

items.says: Name the performance measure, its baseline, and the page or device conditions.
Distinguish the 35% improvement from the separate LCP result.
items.because: The bullets may count the same improvement twice.

items.says: Identify the audit that flagged the 14 issues and how the fixes were verified.
items.because: “All” is a strong claim that needs support.

items.says: Clarify whether the tests caught the regressions in CI or helped identify them another way.
Show that the 60 tests were meaningful cases, not just a test-count metric.
Verify the LCP measurements and the attribution to lazy-loading the hero image.
items.because: Lazy-loading an immediately visible hero image can delay it and worsen LCP, and other changes may have contributed.

items.says: Storing input in React state does not make it safe to render with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: That rendering method bypasses React’s usual escaping and may leave the claimed XSS prevention unsafe.

items.says: Explain the A/B test’s sample size, duration, comparison, and statistical reliability.
items.because: The 9% bookings result needs support.

items.says: Distinguish this page’s result from the other performance claims.
Verify the 400-stop count.
Explain how the 900 weekly riders were measured.
items.because: Analytics may count sessions or requests rather than people.

items.says: Define “opened” and explain the measurement conditions for both load times.
items.because: The device and network conditions should make the comparison like-for-like.

items.says: Verify that the agency link is public and current, and describe it accurately.
items.because: A developer-page link shows visibility, not necessarily agency adoption or endorsement.

items.says: The React and TypeScript contribution conflicts with the project heading’s Vue stack.
items.because: The technologies actually used are unclear.

items.says: Specify your own scope and deliverables in the booking flow.
items.because: The description is broad compared with the calendar bullet.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the calendar component and what its tests covered.
The travel-search bullet does not fit a library room-booking project.
items.because: Its project and ownership are unclear.

items.says: The travel-search result closely repeats the Lumen hotel-search result.
items.because: The apparent duplication raises a credibility concern.

items.says: Put the 2025 internship before the 2023–2024 role.
items.because: The experience section should be reverse chronological.

items.says: “Storybok” is a misspelling of Storybook.
List Angular only if you can defend your proficiency with concrete experience.
items.because: The resume currently gives no evidence for it.

items.says: Make the skills categories consistent.
items.because: The “Methods” label groups practices and technical concepts together.
